# Lead Lab Solution Design: Technology Stack
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent) on behalf of Agno JF

**Technical baseline:** Laravel modular monolith, PHP 8.3 or newer, MySQL 8 or MariaDB 10.6 or newer, Inertia React, TypeScript, shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS v4, private local storage, database-backed search, YouTube embeds, and the existing Apache or Nginx web server with PHP-FPM.

**Decision status:** Adopt this as the build baseline if the environment gate passes. The requester directed this run to use application-managed accounts and defer Microsoft 365 SSO for the MVP. The canonical project register, exact runtime versions, and deployment details still require reconciliation or evidence.

## Stack Decision

| Component | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Application | Laravel modular monolith | Fast delivery, clear conventions, server-side security, and one deployable application |
| Runtime | PHP 8.3 or newer, using the highest supported stable version available | Matches the generated Laravel 13 application requirement while allowing the IT environment to control the exact version |
| Dependency management | Composer | Standard PHP dependency management and repeatable deployments |
| Interface | Inertia React with TypeScript | Keeps Laravel as the monolith while enabling a rich, typed application interface |
| UI components | Official shadcn/ui components with Radix primitives and Lucide icons | Provides accessible, composable components that remain owned in the repository |
| Styling and assets | Tailwind CSS v4 compiled with Vite | Fast responsive layout work with the generated Laravel React toolchain |
| Browser runtime | React 19 with small focused client interactions | Supports desktop, tablet, and mobile without a separate backend service |
| Database | Existing MySQL 8 or MariaDB 10.6 or newer | Fits the approved plan and supports relational content, roles, filters, and activity records |
| Sessions and cache | Database-backed sessions and cache for the single-server MVP | Avoids adding Redis while keeping access state and revocation observable |
| Authentication | Laravel session authentication with administrator-controlled accounts; Microsoft 365 SSO deferred for the MVP by requester direction in this run | Supports restricted access without public registration or a paid identity service |
| Account onboarding | Administrator creates the participant and issues a temporary password; first login requires a password change | Reduces email dependency and keeps participant-data handling within the application |
| Roles | A small role value on the user record plus Laravel policies and gates | Covers participant, moderator, and administrator without adding an unnecessary permissions package |
| File storage | Private local storage outside the public web directory | Prevents direct public URLs and allows an authenticated download handler |
| Search | Indexed database queries across session and material metadata | Meets the MVP search and filter needs without Elasticsearch or another service |
| Video | YouTube privacy-enhanced embed where supported by the selected host | Meets MVP playback while retaining the documented URL-sharing limitation |
| Web server | Existing Apache or Nginx with PHP-FPM | Uses the team-supported server pattern and avoids new infrastructure |
| Deployment | Git source, Composer install, built assets, database migrations, and repeatable server deployment steps | Keeps releases inspectable and reversible |
| Testing | PHPUnit feature tests plus manual staging acceptance checks | Covers authorization, content, downloads, revocation, and responsive workflows with minimal tooling |
| Logging | Framework logs plus an administrative activity table | Supports troubleshooting and the approved audit requirement |
| Cost | Open-source software and existing infrastructure; no paid application dependency | Preserves the zero-license-cost constraint |

## Explicit Non-Choices

- No Next.js SPA for the MVP. Inertia React provides the interface without creating a separate backend service or deployment.
- No microservices. The approved product is one community and the delivery window is short.
- No Redis, Elasticsearch, Docker, Kubernetes, or managed cloud service by default. Add them only if the existing server requires them or an approved change authorizes them.
- No public registration. Access remains administrator-controlled.
- Microsoft 365 SSO is deferred from the MVP by requester direction in this run. Reconcile RQ-18 (Microsoft 365 SSO should be used for the new application) in the canonical project records before launch planning.
- No video hosting or streaming service is introduced. YouTube remains the MVP host, with RQ-17 (embedded video URL protection) tested as a residual-risk condition.

## Core Application Shape

The application will contain one web codebase with these logical areas:

- Access: users, account status, roles, sessions, and password change flow.
- Community: posts, comments, categories, pinned announcements, and moderation actions.
- Classroom: courses, modules, lessons, sessions, video links, and resources.
- Calendar: events, meeting links, dates, and descriptions.
- Administration: members, permissions, content, files, categories, events, and activity logs.
- Operations: health checks, logs, backups, restore evidence, and deployment records.

The application will not use multi-tenant architecture. It will serve one Lead Lab community.

## Vertical Slice Mapping

| Slice step | Planned implementation | Evidence required |
|---|---|---|
| Administrator creates a participant | Admin member screen and user record with disabled-by-default or active status | Admin action and created synthetic account |
| Participant logs in | Laravel session authentication and password-change flow with Inertia React screens | Successful login and first-login password change |
| Unauthenticated visitor is blocked | Route middleware and server-side authorization | Direct request returns the expected denial |
| Administrator publishes one session | Session form with title, category, date, description, video, and resource fields | Published record and visible authenticated session |
| Participant plays video | Authenticated session view with YouTube embed | Staging playback evidence and URL-sharing limitation |
| Participant downloads file | Authenticated download controller reads private storage | Authorized download and unauthorized direct-request denial |
| Administrator revokes access | Account status update and authorization check | Post-revocation request is denied |
| Staging deployment | Existing server deployment method | Source version, deployment record, and staging URL |

## Security Design

- Route, Inertia request, and download authorization will be enforced server-side.
- Passwords will use the selected framework's approved hashing system.
- Forms will use CSRF protection and validation.
- Login attempts will be rate-limited.
- Upload type, size, and storage location will be validated.
- Private files will not be placed in a public web directory.
- Administrative actions will be recorded.
- Database and private files will be backed up and restored in a test before launch.
- HTTPS is required before participant use.

## Build Sequence

1. Confirm the environment gate and authentication or participant-data decision.
2. Create the Laravel application and database migrations.
3. Build the authenticated shell, roles, account lifecycle, and route protection.
4. Build one session, YouTube embed, private resource, and revocation flow.
5. Deploy the vertical slice to staging and run the required tests.
6. Expand to classroom, search, filters, community, calendar, administration, and moderation.
